# Francisco Acosta

> Physics PhD candidate at UC Santa Barbara studying the geometry, symmetry, and dynamics of representations learned by neural networks.

Francisco Acosta is a physicist and computational neuroscientist at the Geometric Intelligence Lab (PI: Nina Miolane) in the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering at UC Santa Barbara. He graduated from MIT in 2021 with an S.B. in Physics.

## Research Focus

His research combines differential geometry, group theory, and computational statistics to understand neural representations:

1. **Riemannian geometry of neural representations** — quantifying the geometric structure (intrinsic and extrinsic curvature) of neural manifolds in both biological and artificial systems.
2. **Task structure and RNN dynamics** — how task structure shapes the dynamics and learned representations of recurrent neural networks, including mechanisms of timescale learning.
3. **Group theory in neural networks** — how neural networks learn and exploit group-theoretic structure inherent in their tasks, with applications to path integration and grid cell emergence.

## Key Publications

- Marchetti, G., Kunin, D., Myers, A., Acosta, F., Miolane, N. (2026). Sequential Group Composition: A Window into the Mechanics of Deep Learning. ICML.
- Acosta, F., Bertics, A., Dinc, F., Miolane, N. (2026). The Timescale Matching Hypothesis in Task-Trained Recurrent Neural Networks. Under review.
- Delikkaya, N. E., Cimen, A., Acosta, F., Myers, A., Alexander, A., Dinc, F., Miolane, N. (2025). Dimensionality of population-level latent mechanisms encoding spatial representations. NeurReps.
- Acosta, F., Dinc, F., Redman, W., Madhav, M., Klindt, D., Miolane, N. (2024). Global Distortions from Local Rewards: Neural Coding Strategies in Path-Integrating Neural Systems. NeurIPS.
- Redman, W., Acosta, F., Acosta-Mendoza, S., Miolane, N. (2024). Not so Griddy: Internal Representations of RNNs Path Integrating More than One Agent. NeurIPS.
- Acosta, F., Sanborn, S., Dao Duc, K., Madhav, M., Miolane, N. (2023). Quantifying Extrinsic Curvature in Neural Manifolds. CVPR Workshop.
- Acosta, F., Conwell, C., Klindt, D., Miolane, N. (2023). Relating Representational Geometry to Cortical Geometry in Visual Cortex. NeurIPS Workshop.

## Software

- Geomstats: contributor to the Python package for Riemannian geometry in ML (github.com/geomstats/geomstats)
- Group AGF: research code for sequential group composition experiments related to the ICML 2026 paper (github.com/geometric-intelligence/group-agf)
